title: Radius-Adaptive Honest Intervals for a Gini-Type Pairwise CATE Functional
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field). Not salvageable within scope. Math and decision panels pass with no findings; independent validity gate recommends downgraded archival.
gap_reasons: The delivered result determines polynomial radius regimes through a logarithmically separated bracket; it does not determine exact pointwise logarithms or whether adaptation necessarily incurs a divergent cost, and the framing preserves these distinctions without a stale matched-frontier claim. Its scope remains a known-uniform two-dimensional randomized binary Lipschitz benchmark, with no normalized-Gini interval theorem or coverage result for the motivating clinical analyses. The specified interval returns [0,1/2] for every n below 2^{2^{40}}, and its exhaustive calibration establishes computability without providing a practically usable inference method or a nontrivial finite-sample demonstration. The constrained-moment donor's displayed formula is supported by [Canonne et al. (2022), Theorem 12](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v178/canonne22a/canonne22a.pdf), but the manuscript should identify that exact source explicitly at the leaf lemma. The projected score is constrained by the specialized experiment, unresolved exact orders, and the distance between the prospective calibration motivation and the delivered procedure's practical performance. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Derived an all-radius logarithmically separated honest-length bracket and radius-blind interval for pair-Gini CATE dispersion in the known-uniform two-dimensional binary Lipschitz model. Official-source attestation, duplicate-theorem removal, fine-residual repair, and explicit Poisson-to-fixed-count TV division led to math and decision PASS with no findings; an independent targeted audit supports downgraded archival. The field floor was not met (achieved subfield); exact logarithms and adaptation cost, practical calibration below n0=2^(2^40), normalized-Gini guarantees, and broader applications remain open, and no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: The proved all-radius result is the two-sided logarithmically separated bracket \(cF_n(r;b_n)\le L_n(r)\le CF_n(r;u_n)\) for ambient-honest expected interval length in the declared randomized binary Lipschitz experiment. One computable radius-blind interval attains the upper envelope simultaneously, with finite-sample honesty, terminating rational calibration, public constants and the specified small-sample fallback. Original-record supported mixtures prove the lower envelope on the same full law class. The switched positive-polynomial coarse statistic and independent fine residual certificate establish the upper bound, including nearly homogeneous benefits. The polynomial homogeneity plateau, interpolation and global saturation are proved bracket consequences, and the same interval gives the adaptation upper comparison. Exact pointwise logarithms and exact adaptation order remain the two explicit open questions. Average effect may have either sign in the full model; normalized benefit summaries have a separate positive-average interpretation. The clinical application motivates prospective calibration of conditional mean-benefit dispersion.
gap: Integrated absolute-value estimation and tolerant testing supply the closest mechanisms. Their verified scopes do not establish connected finite-sample honest intervals with localized expected length for this pairwise CATE functional on one fixed Lipschitz class.
fill: The theorem-level kernel keeps the full class and original records, combines two independently calibrated resolutions, and compares supported mixtures across every radius. Its public calibration and uniform constants are part of the result to prove. The logarithmic bracket supports a specialized subfield paper; no general replacement for tolerant testing or nonsmooth-functional theory is claimed.
